title: Déjà Vu
text: “Where is Naofumi? After brainwashing the people and throwing the country into chaos… Well, never mind. Motoyasu! I’m going to defeat you!”
“So, was that whispered to you by the Three Heroes Church?”

“‘Whispered’ sounds a bit rude. I was asked by the king and the princess. Second Princess Melty, who had gone there to foster friendly relations, was kidnapped by Naofumi and Motoyasu. They asked me to please rescue her!”

Well, well—it’s exactly as my Father said. How simple-minded. You really ought to learn to be a little more skeptical of your country and religion. Well, he is an Itsuki, after all. This guy just wants to satisfy his own sense of justice—that’s all that matters to him, more than his comrades. It’s quite ridiculous, considering that in the future, he tried to use that very power of brainwashing to rule Melromarc.

“My sense of justice whispers to me that you lot are evil. This time, I won’t lose! I’m on the side of justice! It’s my duty—as a hero myself—to condemn the heroes who have strayed onto the path of evil!”

Who’s saying that? The ones crying crocodile tears behind you are the true evil. Evil lurks behind the facade of justice. Indeed, evil takes root precisely among those who put on a righteous front. I suppose you call true righteousness “justice,” but there’s a saying that goes like this:
“The victor is the government; the vanquished is the rebel. To claim that justice is right and obvious to everyone is childish logic.”
Even I can understand that. After all, Itsuki’s sense of justice is sloppy. Even things that seem right at first glance become clear when you look at how they play out later.
“I bet even the cases the Three Heroes Church solved were later blamed on my Father… because the Shield Hero got involved, things got worse, and Itsuki was impeached for it, right?”

“That’s right! Admitting you know that is the same as admitting it! Even though we went to the trouble of solving them, I heard things got worse later because Naofumi interfered! Those evil heroes—no, those Demon Lords—who seek to rule the world!　I, the true Hero, will put an end to them right here!”
“Hahahah! Do you really think someone like Itsuki is capable of that?”
I step down from Yuki-chan and turn around. Running away would be easy. But according to my Father, Itsuki’s life is likely in danger as well. If Takt comes, it’ll be a real mess.
It’s also true that it would be a hassle if Itsuki were killed. The previous loop speaks for itself. I, Motoyasu, will never give up, but it’s also true that this would cause trouble for my Father.
All right, then. For the sake of the future, I suppose I should let Itsuki know right here who’s the boss.
“There’s no way I can’t do this! Motoyasu! Your evil deeds end right here!”

Itsuki furrows his brow and draws his bow, while his companions step forward. Ah, as expected, the Smoked Meat I blew up isn’t here. Even so, it seems the lineup is more or less the same as in the previous loop.
Oh my, that’s the green stalker pig. If I recall correctly, that guy was supposed to be dumped by Itsuki. But that’s irrelevant now.
“Well then, let’s get started. Ah, I’d like Yuki-chan and the others to just watch quietly. This is nothing that warrants bothering them.”
“Understood.”
“Eh… Kou wants to play too.”
“You’ll have to hold back.”
It’s dangerous if Itsuki goes too far, after all. I’ll need to keep him in check. Just how strong is Itsuki these days? I’d estimate around 70, I suppose.
Well, either way, he’s practically a pushover to me. The dragons deep in the mountains of Siltvelt would probably put up a better fight.

Ah… When I think back to the fight between my Father and Itsuki a month and a half ago, I’m reminded once again just how incredible Father’s skill is. He defeated Itsuki without even showing his true strength.

The fact that he subdued Itsuki with just his formidable Defense Power makes it hard to fully grasp, face-to-face, just how much power lies dormant within him. If I’d unleashed a powerful Skill right there in the castle courtyard, their alertness would’ve spiked instantly. But I suppose they figured that since I was just “tough,” all they had to do was break through my defenses.
“You can only underestimate me for so long!”

Ah, my future Father would probably grumble something like that. He’d say that, in this scenario, I’m the one who looks like the villain. After all, I do possess immense power, and I’m trying to take on a group of them all by myself. I’m not too familiar with anime, but I remember something a literature-loving pig used to say back in the day.

That this is what a story where justice triumphs is supposed to be like. But this is reality, and here, victory is justice. Is someone who challenges a stronger opponent with sheer numbers really on the side of justice? If you look at it another way, it just seems like a despicable and cowardly act.
Let’s try imitating my future Father here. It’ll be better for Itsuki, too.
“Itsuki, someone like you is no match for me alone. I’ll render scum like you incapable of fighting in a matter of seconds.”
“You said it! I… Justice will never lose!”
The moment Itsuki fires his arrow, his companions charge toward me.
“Aiming Lancer III!”
I hurl my lance high into the sky, making it rain down all around them!
“‘‘‘Waaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!’’’’
Just that alone was enough to blow Itsuki’s companions right out of the way. After all of them were sent flying through the air, they’re now sprawled out on the ground.
“You’re a decade too early to be challenging me with something this pathetic.”

Huh? Is this déjà vu? This scene… it rings a bell. I’m pretty sure I was blown away just like this when I challenged that translucent pig with the fan. What a twist of fate. Who would’ve thought I’d end up with the same result as that translucent pig this time?

Come to think of it, that translucent pig hasn’t shown up yet. I really should be on guard against it… but well, I suppose it’s thanks to how quickly I took care of the wave. Itsuki is looking around in utter shock at how all his companions were wiped out in an instant.
“Huh? Huh? T-that can’t be!?”
“Well then, next up is Itsuki… it’s your turn. Paralyze Lance!”
Taking care not to go too hard, I quickly closed in on Itsuki and thrust my lance into him. It seems Itsuki wasn’t even able to dodge the attack.
“Ugh… I’m not done yet!”
“Oh? It seems you’ve boosted your resistance.”

Losing to Father must have prompted a shift in his strategy. No, it’s more likely he’s adapting his strategy to match a battle against his Father. The paralyzed Itsuki is slowly getting back to his feet. Oh well… I suppose I’ll have to unleash a slightly stronger paralysis skill, then?
“Teleport—”
What? He’s retreating? This is ridiculous. Does he really think I’d let him get away that easily? Yes, this is a battle from which there’s no escape.
“I won’t let you get away. Here comes Silence Lance V!”
Oh, it seems he’s surprised to be silenced. However, with Itsuki having strengthened his resistance, I’m not sure how long the effect will last. He’s undoubtedly taken some sort of antidote as well.
Even after being hit with a V-level spell, he shows no signs of giving up and is reaching for an item. Well then, I’ll do my part to prevent his escape.
I’m beginning my Magic spellcasting. Itsuki is hurriedly pulling out an item to break the Silence. He’s put some distance between himself and his fallen comrade—I wonder what he plans to do with him.

What do you think he’d do if I started taking out Itsuki’s allies one by one right here? After all, to Itsuki, his allies are nothing more than pawns that exist solely to praise him. Well, if I did something like that, I’d end up being hated not only by my Father but by Filo-tan as well. After all, I promised with all my heart and soul to save the world for Filo-tan and my Father.
“Liberation Firefield V!”

This is a Magic spell that creates a zone that amplifies the effects of fire. Normally, it falls under the category of Ceremonial Magic or Cooperative Magic, but my goal here is to disrupt the teleportation skill. Well, it’s a simple Magic spell—if they use the teleportation skill a few times, they’ll escape—but that much time is more than enough.
“That’s it. After ‘Lightning Spear IV,’ here comes ‘Paralyze Lance VI’!”
I closed the distance in an instant, grazed the fleeing Itsuki with an electrified “Lightning Spear” to make him stagger, and then deeply paralyzed him with “Paralyze Lance.”
“Guaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!”
Itsuki recoiled and collapsed with a thud. He’s crackling slightly from the electric shock. Now for the rest…
“T-this is… ridiculous… This is practically… cheating…”
“Anyone stronger than you is cheating, after all. Here comes Sleep Spear V.”

I delivered a sharp jab to induce sleep and make him lose consciousness. Glancing around, I saw Itsuki’s companions trying to get back up. Considering my last run, killing them would be an option, but Father warned me that it would put me at a disadvantage later when I reveal the truth to Itsuki. I’ll just ignore them.

However, I can’t just leave Itsuki here. Even without Smoked Meat, they might try to kill a defeated Itsuki. I’ll kick Itsuki so he rolls over, then hook his collar with the spear’s ferrule and hoist him up.
“Kou, I’m going to take him as a souvenir for my Father.”
“Okay! Got it!”
I’ll load the limp Itsuki onto Kou’s back.
“Ha ha ha! Itsuki has fallen into my hands! Well then, farewell!”
Perched on Yuki-chan’s back, I declare triumphantly.
“B-bweh! B-b-bweh!”
One of Itsuki’s companions—a greenish pig—is reaching out and squealing. That’s the Stalker Pig. Is it really stalking Itsuki? I have no idea.
“Ha ha ha! Your sense of justice is pretty obvious, isn’t it?”
“Let’s get going!”
Yuki-chan took off running, carrying me—who couldn’t stop laughing—and we made a beeline for the exit. And just like that, I succeeded in capturing Itsuki alive.
